text_first_900: A curved surface has a flat tangent plane at each smooth point. This plane describes the directions of motion available locally along the surface.  Changing one surface coordinate while holding the other fixed traces a curve. The two coordinate derivatives give tangent vectors that span the plane wherever they are independent.  These basis vectors can change with position and need not be perpendicular or have unit length. Combining them lets physicists describe velocities and other tangent quantities on curved surfaces without relying on fixed Cartesian directions.

text_first_900: The #NobelPrize in Chemistry 2026 recognises discoveries that have enabled chemists to drive chemical reactions that lead to homochirality.  Life’s chemistry is what chemists call homochiral, after the Greek words for “same” and “hand”. Like hands, all amino acids exist as two mirrored variants, but only one of them is found in the proteins in your cells. The other is rarely found in nature.  For a long time, chemists wondered how homochirality can emerge. When they began to experiment with chemical reactions that can form two mirrored molecules, they always obtained equal proportions of both in their test tubes. However, chemists strived to produce only one of these mirror images, because in the development of molecules that will interact with living beings – such as in pharmaceuticals – only one mirror image will have the desired effect. text_first_900: Differentiation turns into multiplication by s. Convolution collapses into an ordinary product.  The Laplace transform does not remove the physics of a system. It relocates it. Linear combinations stay linear: ℒ{af(t) + bg(t)} = aF(s) + bG(s).  A delay of a seconds multiplies the transform by e^(−as). The derivative f′(t) becomes sF(s) − f(0), so initial conditions enter as simple subtractions. And the convolution f ∗ g is exactly F(s)G(s). What required integrals and derivatives in time is now arithmetic in s.  Four rules, and the language of dynamics becomes algebra.

text_first_900: Fibonacci numbers hide inside a hyperbolic sine: Fₘ = 2/(√5 iᵐ) · sinh(m log(iφ)).  It is Binet's formula in disguise. Since log(iφ) = ln φ + iπ/2, expanding sinh gives Fₘ = (φᵐ − ψᵐ)/√5 with φ = (1 + √5)/2 and ψ = −1/φ.  The formula never asks m to be a whole number. For real m it returns a complex value whose real part is a smooth wave through 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, and backwards through 1, −1, 2, −3, 5, since F₋ₘ = (−1)ᵐ⁺¹ Fₘ.

text_first_900: Quarks are not observed in isolation because the strong interaction confines color charge inside color-neutral hadrons.  Separating quarks forms a narrow color-flux tube whose energy grows approximately with distance. Pulling harder eventually creates a quark-antiquark pair, breaking the tube into new hadrons rather than releasing a free quark. This process is seen experimentally as jets of color-neutral particles. The Cornell potential models short-distance attraction plus long-distance confinement, while the underlying theory is quantum chromodynamics.
